mappings.note: Matches four nitrogen-cycle processes to their descriptions - microbial interactions in an ecosystem (C4.3). Not LO-56: a matching table is not a flow chart drawn by the student, which is the line I hold for LO-56 throughout.

Turns entirely on insolation at the surface being less than the solar constant because the atmosphere absorbs and scatters. That is the nature and fate of the incoming beam - LO-2. LO-3 is out: no band is singled out, the loss is across the board.

Three statements to be judged, each one a definition of a sphere (geosphere, cryosphere, biosphere). LO-55 is the only code in the frame that names them, and this is pure sphere identification with no process attached.

Numerical: intensity x area x time. LO-2 supplies the insolation quantity; C8.1 supplies the mathematical model used to predict a result. This calculation demand is what separates it from O4 and V62, which only recall the solar constant's value.

Eutrophication read off a diagram: the chain runs nutrients to algae to oxygen loss to fish death, i.e. interactions inside an aquatic ecosystem (C4.3). C2.8 carries the agricultural-runoff cause, which no outcome names.

Ordering troposphere to exosphere is pure structural recall of the atmosphere. POOR FIT: the frame has no outcome for atmospheric layering, so only the competency - which names the atmosphere as a system - is available.

Planetary winds are 'air movement', LO-5's own example. POOR FIT on the actual discriminator, which is Coriolis deflection by the Earth's rotation; rotation appears in no outcome in this frame (LO-4 names tilt, latitude and shape, not spin).

Asks for the UV band's wavelength range - nothing but frequency/wavelength discrimination, which is LO-3's whole content. Not LO-2: the item never mentions how much radiation arrives or reaches the surface.

The Reason clause is ozone absorbing UV specifically (LO-3, band-selective absorption); the Assertion is about the absence of vertical mixing, i.e. air movement (LO-5). Both are needed because the item is scored on whether R explains A.

Four albedo values in a table; pick the lowest. Surface-property interaction with solar radiation, LO-5. Shares its outcome with the rest of the albedo family - honestly so, since the frame has no albedo-specific outcome to split them by.

Orders the electromagnetic spectrum by wavelength. LO-56 also names the electromagnetic spectrum, but its verb is 'Draw' and this item only sorts a supplied list, so LO-3 - radiation as waves of different frequencies - is the right one.

Saline water becoming denser and sinking. POOR FIT: this is a hydrosphere process with no solar-radiation or differential-heating element at all, and the frame's only reference to the hydrosphere is inside the competency text.

Find the false statement about mountain and valley breezes - LO-5 names both by name. Distinguished from its siblings only by being a negative-stem MCQ; the outcome is genuinely shared across the whole breeze family.

Two material blocks classified by how much radiation each reflects. Same LO-5 surface clause as O3 and O14; the item differs only in stimulus format, and no sibling outcome distinguishes reading a block diagram from reading a table.

Asks for the ecological consequence of nitrate runoff (algal bloom, oxygen depletion) - C4.3's ecosystem interactions. Paired with O9, which asks for the same chain's CAUSE; both honestly share the outcome because the frame has no nutrient-pollution outcome.

Venus vs Mercury: the point is that an atmosphere re-traps what the surface absorbed and re-radiated - LO-5's interaction clause applied off-planet. Not LO-4: the false lead is distance from the Sun, not shape, latitude or tilt.

The slow carbon cycle: burial into fossil fuels and carbonate shells sinking to the sea floor. Those reservoirs are the geosphere and hydrosphere, named only in C2.8. C4.3 covers the marine-organism statement. My fast/slow rule sends slow-cycle items to C2.8.

Identifies the troposphere from a lapse-rate table (no outcome covers layer structure, hence C2.8), and the correct option's justification is 'weather forms as warm air rises' - LO-5's air-movement clause.

Which gas is not a greenhouse gas. POOR FIT: recall of atmospheric composition and gas identity. No outcome in this frame names greenhouse gases at all; the greenhouse effect is only reachable through LO-5's re-radiation clause, which this item does not test.

Applies the albedo relation to a design decision (paint roofs light). LO-5 supplies the science; C2.8 carries the deliberate human intervention in the Earth system, which separates it from the descriptive albedo items like O14 and O18.

The Reason clause is transpiration reducing atmospheric moisture - LO-5's 'evaporation' is the only outcome word that reaches moisture flux. C2.8 carries the biosphere-to-atmosphere link. Not C4.3: no organism-level interaction is being analysed.

Matches four spheres to their components. LO-55's surviving fragment is a list of exactly these spheres, so it is a direct hit; no process, no radiation and no cycle appears, so nothing else in the frame competes.

The five events to be ordered are sorted BY BAND - UV stopped high up, visible reaching the ground, infrared going back out and being trapped - so LO-3 leads. LO-5 covers the surface absorbing and re-radiating in the middle of that sequence.

Four statements running glaciers to sea level to soil to ocean acidity - a cryosphere/hydrosphere/geosphere/biosphere chain, which only LO-55 names. Distinguished from N3 (water cycle mechanism) by being a sphere-by-sphere impact audit.

Identifies two arrows as incoming shortwave visible and outgoing longwave infrared - a pure band discrimination (LO-3) about radiation meeting the surface (LO-5). The diagram is stimulus only, so C8.1 is not invoked.
